sections.h2: What must be ready before a fast Elk Grove Village closing?
sections.html:
The village requires a transfer stamp, a settled water account and a few forms before a sale can close, so a fast sale in Elk Grove Village depends on lining up those items early. The Census Bureau estimates 31,885 residents for July 1, 2025, living in a village that sits next to O'Hare International Airport and handles its own transfer tax.

Elk Grove Village lies in both Cook and DuPage counties, and the county of your parcel decides where the deed is recorded. A title company or attorney usually files the paperwork, yet you should know what they will ask you for.

  • Your parcel number and the county on your tax bill.
  • The names on the deed, spelled exactly as recorded, including middle initials and trust numbers.
  • A final water meter reading booked ahead of closing.
  • A mortgage payoff statement and a list of any liens.
  • For homes north of Elk Grove Boulevard, the underground fuel tank disclosure form.

sections.h2: How does the Elk Grove Village transfer stamp work?
sections.html:
Elk Grove Village levies its own tax when title to local real estate changes hands: $3 for every $1,000 of value, counting any fraction, with the seller carrying primary liability. To buy the stamp you submit a village Real Estate Tax Declaration Form with two signatures, a copy of the new deed, a water and sewer affidavit, and either the state PTAX-203 or an EZ Dec form. An unsigned copy of the deed is accepted for purchase, but a copy of the signed deed must reach the Finance Department within 10 days after closing.

Acceptable payment is cash, a cashier's check, a money order, or an attorney's or title company's check made out to Elk Grove Village. It does not accept credit cards or personal and company checks. The finance counter in the Municipal Building, 901 Wellington Avenue, sells stamps on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30, and finished forms can be emailed to fc@elkgrove.org. Mailed requests take about one week, so leave extra time if your closing is close.

The Finance Department's number is (847) 439-3900.

sections.h2: What water bill steps come before closing in Elk Grove Village?
sections.html:
The village requires the final water bill to be paid when you buy the transfer stamp, and it asks that a final meter reading be scheduled at least two days before the closing date. All other utility bills and debts owed to the village must also be settled before the stamp is issued. The water and sewer affidavit asks for the top three lines, the seller's forwarding address and the buyer's name.

Because the stamp, the final reading and the payoff all need to land near the closing date, put the reading on the calendar as soon as the closing is set. A seller who forgets the reading can delay the stamp, and a delayed stamp can delay the closing. Ask your title company to confirm that the village has the reading scheduled.

sections.h2: What fuel tank disclosure applies in Elk Grove Village?
sections.html:
The village requires a Real Estate Disclosure Form for underground fuel heating storage tanks on all properties located north of Elk Grove Boulevard. Sellers must give it to the buyers, and it covers the possible presence of those tanks. The village directs questions about underground heating fuel tanks to the Fire Department at (847) 734-8020.

This requirement is easy to overlook because it applies by location inside the village. Check where your street sits relative to Elk Grove Boulevard, and fill the form out before the contract date rather than at the closing table. A house with a known tank history can still sell, but the buyer should receive the information up front.

sections.h2: Are there exemptions or refunds on the Elk Grove Village transfer tax?
sections.html:
Certain transfers are exempt. The village points sellers to Village Code 3-2-5-F and the back of the declaration form for the complete list, and anyone claiming an exemption must supply proof of every fact needed to establish it. The exempt stamp carries a $10 handling fee, and all utility bills and village debts must be paid before it is issued.

Some taxpayers can claim a refund on a portion of the tax. Applications for re-investment or senior refunds must reach the village within one year of payment, so keep your receipt and closing documents. The village's Real Estate Transfer Stamp Refund and Exemption pages describe who qualifies. If you are transferring a house into a trust or between family members, ask the Finance Department whether the exempt route fits before you purchase a regular stamp.

  • Exemption claims need proof of each fact behind the exemption.
  • The exempt stamp carries a $10 handling fee.
  • Re-investment and senior refund requests must arrive within one year of payment.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell in Elk Grove Village, and what do the Census numbers say?
sections.html:
Elk Grove Village was incorporated on July 17, 1956 as a planned suburb about 22 miles northwest of Chicago. Centex built most of the early houses, and the village kept residential areas separate from a large industrial park on its eastern edge. That park covers 5.9 square miles, holds nearly 3,600 businesses and employs nearly 100,000 people, which makes it the largest consolidated business park in North America. Alexian Brothers Medical Center is the largest single employer, with more than 2,200 workers.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and neighborhoods shape a sale in Elk Grove Village?
sections.html:
Interstate 290 splits the school boundaries. East of I-290, students attend Elk Grove High School in Illinois High School District 214 and Community Consolidated School District 59. West of I-290, students go to James B. Conant High School in Township High School District 211 and Mead Junior High in District 54. Name the right district in your listing, since buyers with children search by it.

The village is reached by I-90, I-290, I-355, Route 53 and IL-390, and the I-490 Western O'Hare Bypass is expected to serve it once complete. Pace Route 223 links to the Rosemont station. Early boundaries ran along Higgins Road, Arlington Heights Road, Landmeier Road and Wildwood Road, and the village doubled in size during the 1960s. The village sits directly beside O'Hare International Airport, and its location along the Golden Corridor is a selling point for commuters.

Deeds are recorded by the Cook County Clerk or the DuPage County Recorder. Cook lists state transfer tax at .50 per $500, county tax at .25 per $500 and a $107 deed recording fee under its April 2024 schedule. DuPage's Recorder keeps records back to 1839 and can be reached at 630-407-5400.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Elk Grove Village?
faqs.a: The village rate is $3 per $1,000 of value, or fraction thereof, with the primary liability on the seller. State and county transfer taxes are separate charges set by the recording county. Ask your title company to list each one on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Can I pay for an Elk Grove Village transfer stamp with a credit card?
faqs.a: No. Cash, a cashier's check, a money order, or an attorney's or title company's check to the village will work. It does not accept credit cards or personal or company checks.

faqs.q: How early must I schedule the final water reading?
faqs.a: The village's stamp page says at least two days before the closing date. Book the reading as soon as your closing date is set, and confirm the timing with the Finance Department.

faqs.q: Do I need an underground fuel tank disclosure?
faqs.a: Yes, if the house is north of Elk Grove Boulevard. The village requires sellers there to give buyers a disclosure form about possible underground fuel heating storage tanks. Fire Department staff answer questions about the tanks.

faqs.q: Which county records my Elk Grove Village deed?
faqs.a: Either Cook County or DuPage County, depending on where your parcel sits. Look at the tax bill for the county, and the title company files the deed there.
